diagnosis.root_cause: Evening oversubscription and contention on shared PON port EPON0/7. Port traffic reaches 912 Mbps currently and peaks at 948 Mbps against roughly 1 Gbps shared capacity, matching the time-dependent slowdown. The subscriber's optical link, ONU, authentication, VLAN, router, and OLT are healthy.
evidence: Subscriber RX power is -21.27 dBm live and remained around -21 dBm for seven days, which is normal and not declining.
Subscriber TX power is about 2.37 dBm, TX bias stayed near 11 mA, and distance remained constant at 167, ruling out laser degradation, fibre degradation, and distance change.
All probed peers on EPON0/7 are online and have normal optical readings, so there is no ONU, splitter, or shared optical outage.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and subtree queries; all eight PONs are reported healthy and OLT metrics are within acceptable operating range.
The router heartbeat is current and healthy.

The subscriber has a valid, CRM-consistent RADIUS entry, correct line ID, normal VLAN 1017, and only two sessions in 24 hours with an average duration of 711 minutes, ruling out authentication flapping.
The PON port carries 912 Mbps currently with a 948 Mbps peak and a 488 Mbps average, indicating near-capacity shared-port contention consistent with evening-only degradation.
The complaint affects perceived throughput rather than optical availability, and the direct shared-port traffic evidence supports PON congestion.

remediation.action: Monitor EPON0/7 utilization and queue/discard rates during the evening peak, then relieve contention by moving customers to another PON, splitting the splitter/PON load, or upgrading capacity where available. Review per-subscriber traffic and apply appropriate QoS or capacity planning. Do not replace the subscriber ONU or fibre based on the current evidence.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and its evening load is reaching 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average, close to the port's shared capacity ceiling. Throughput degrades for everyone on the port during peak hours. No optical or authentication fault exists.
expected_reasoning: The complaint is time-of-day specific, which points at load rather than at a physical fault
RX is flat at -21.2 dBm inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe shows every ONU on the port online with normal optical readings
RADIUS is clean and sessions are long and stable, so authentication is not involved
PON port traffic is at 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average
Daily traffic for this customer is roughly three times the network mean and rising, not falling
Every fault-driven degradation reduces traffic; congestion raises it, so the direction is the discriminator
The customer's own throughput series drops sharply during the same evening hours each day
The port carries 47 customers, at the top of the observed occupancy distribution
This is capacity exhaustion on a shared port, not a fault on any one line

expected_escalation.review_reason: EPON0/7 needs a capacity review; 47 customers on one port with evening load near ceiling

distractors: Multi-customer slowness resembles a splitter or feeder degradation
Elevated OLT CPU and temperature could be read as device stress causing the slowness
Reduced throughput in the speed series looks like a link problem
